catalog.name: Air Quality & Atmospheric Pollution
catalog.description: Comprehensive air quality monitoring datasets from multiple NASA satellite missions providing essential information for atmospheric pollution assessment, environmental health monitoring, and air quality management. These products combine ground-level pollutants, aerosols, and trace gases critical for understanding air quality impacts on human health and ecosystems.

info.name: Attribution
info.content: Data from NASA satellite missions including MERRA-2, TEMPO, MOPITT, OMI, MODIS, and VIIRS. Processing by NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, Jet Propulsion Laboratory, and Langley Research Center. Contact: earthdata-support@nasa.gov

info.name: License
info.content: NASA data is generally available for public use. Air quality products are designed for environmental monitoring, public health applications, and pollution source identification.

info.name: Health Applications
info.content: Essential for air quality index calculation, health risk assessment, pollution exposure monitoring, and environmental health research supporting public health decision-making.

info.name: Environmental Applications
info.content: Critical for emission inventory validation, pollution transport studies, environmental impact assessment, and air quality management policy development.

members.name: Trace Gas Pollutants
members.description: Major atmospheric trace gas pollutants including carbon monoxide, sulfur dioxide, and ozone affecting air quality and human health at local to global scales.

members.name: Carbon Monoxide Emissions (Monthly)
members.description: Monthly carbon monoxide emissions from MERRA-2 reanalysis, representing CO emissions from combustion sources including vehicles, industry, and biomass burning affecting urban and regional air quality.

info.name: Background
info.content: Carbon monoxide (CO) is a toxic gas produced by incomplete combustion of fossil fuels, biomass burning, and industrial processes. It is a key air pollutant affecting human health and an important precursor to ground-level ozone formation.

info.name: Health Significance
info.content: CO reduces oxygen-carrying capacity of blood, causing cardiovascular stress, reduced cognitive function, and at high concentrations can be fatal. Particularly dangerous in enclosed spaces and urban environments.

info.name: Source Categories
info.content: Major sources include vehicle exhaust, industrial combustion, residential heating, wildfire smoke, and agricultural burning

info.name: Spatial Resolution
info.content: 0.5° × 0.625° global grid suitable for regional air quality assessment and emission inventory validation

info.name: Units
info.content: kg m⁻² s⁻¹ representing emission flux of carbon monoxide to the atmosphere

info.name: Air Quality Applications
info.content: Urban air quality monitoring, emission inventory validation, pollution source identification, transportation planning, industrial emission assessment

info.name: Climate Applications
info.content: Atmospheric chemistry studies, ozone precursor analysis, biomass burning impact assessment, emission trend analysis

info.name: Policy Applications
info.content: Emission reduction strategy evaluation, air quality standard compliance monitoring, environmental health policy development

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA MERRA-2 atmospheric chemistry reanalysis, NASA Global Modeling and Assimilation Office

members.name: Carbon Monoxide Total Column (Daily)
members.description: Daily carbon monoxide total atmospheric column from MOPITT satellite observations, providing comprehensive global CO distribution for air quality and pollution transport monitoring.

info.name: Background
info.content: MOPITT (Measurements of Pollution in the Troposphere) provides daily global measurements of carbon monoxide throughout the atmospheric column, enabling detection of pollution plumes, biomass burning events, and long-range transport of CO.

info.name: Measurement Technique
info.content: Uses thermal infrared spectroscopy to measure CO absorption, providing vertical profile information and total column amounts with high sensitivity to tropospheric CO

info.name: Spatial Resolution
info.content: 22 km × 22 km footprint with daily global coverage, excellent for tracking pollution events and transport patterns

info.name: Temporal Coverage
info.content: March 2000 to present, providing over 20 years of global CO observations for trend analysis and climatological studies

info.name: Units
info.content: molecules cm⁻² representing total atmospheric column abundance of carbon monoxide

info.name: Pollution Monitoring
info.content: Excellent for detecting urban pollution, industrial emissions, wildfire smoke, agricultural burning, and transboundary pollution transport

info.name: Event Detection
info.content: Capable of detecting major pollution events, forest fires, volcanic emissions, and seasonal pollution patterns with daily temporal resolution

info.name: Validation Applications
info.content: Used to validate atmospheric chemistry models, emission inventories, and ground-based air quality measurements

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA Terra MOPITT mission, University of Toronto, National Center for Atmospheric Research

members.name: Sulfur Dioxide Column Density (Monthly)
members.description: Monthly sulfur dioxide column mass density from MERRA-2 reanalysis, representing SO2 concentrations from industrial sources, volcanic emissions, and fossil fuel combustion affecting air quality and acid deposition.

info.name: Background
info.content: Sulfur dioxide (SO2) is a major air pollutant released from fossil fuel burning, industrial processes, and volcanic activity. It contributes to acid rain formation, particulate matter production, and respiratory health problems.

info.name: Health Impacts
info.content: SO2 causes respiratory irritation, exacerbates asthma and other lung diseases, and contributes to cardiovascular problems. Particularly harmful to children, elderly, and individuals with pre-existing respiratory conditions.

info.name: Environmental Impacts
info.content: Major contributor to acid deposition affecting forests, lakes, and buildings. Precursor to sulfate aerosols that affect climate and visibility.

info.name: Source Categories
info.content: Primary sources include coal-fired power plants, industrial smelting, petroleum refining, volcanic eruptions, and ship emissions

info.name: Units
info.content: kg m⁻² representing column integrated mass of sulfur dioxide in the atmospheric column

info.name: Monitoring Applications
info.content: Industrial emission monitoring, volcanic eruption tracking, power plant pollution assessment, ship emission surveillance, acid rain precursor analysis

info.name: Regulatory Applications
info.content: Clean air act compliance monitoring, emission reduction strategy evaluation, environmental health risk assessment

info.name: Research Applications
info.content: Atmospheric chemistry studies, aerosol formation research, climate impact assessment, air quality model validation

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA MERRA-2 atmospheric chemistry analysis, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center

members.name: Ozone & UV Monitoring
members.description: Ozone and ultraviolet radiation monitoring from advanced satellite instruments providing high-resolution air quality assessment over North America and UV exposure monitoring.

members.name: TEMPO Ozone & UV Index
members.description: High-resolution ozone and UV aerosol index from TEMPO (Tropospheric Emissions: Monitoring of Pollution) satellite providing hourly air quality monitoring over North America for public health and environmental applications.

info.name: Background
info.content: TEMPO is NASA's first Earth Venture Instrument providing hourly observations of air quality over North America from geostationary orbit, offering unprecedented temporal resolution for pollution monitoring and public health applications.

info.name: Revolutionary Capabilities
info.content: First space-based instrument to monitor air quality hourly during daytime, enabling tracking of pollution evolution, rush hour impacts, and rapid response to air quality events

info.name: Spatial Coverage
info.content: North American domain from Mexico to Canada with 2.1 km × 4.4 km spatial resolution at nadir, providing city-scale air quality monitoring

info.name: Temporal Resolution
info.content: Hourly observations during daylight hours, revolutionizing our ability to track diurnal air quality patterns and rapid pollution changes

info.name: Ozone Monitoring
info.content: Measures tropospheric ozone column amounts, enabling ground-level ozone estimation and air quality index calculation for public health warnings

info.name: UV Aerosol Index
info.content: Detects absorbing aerosols including dust, smoke, and volcanic ash that affect air quality and UV radiation reaching the surface

info.name: Public Health Applications
info.content: Real-time air quality alerts, AQI forecasting, pollution exposure assessment, health risk communication, environmental justice studies

info.name: Urban Applications
info.content: City-scale pollution monitoring, traffic impact assessment, industrial emission tracking, urban planning support

info.name: Emergency Response
info.content: Wildfire smoke tracking, industrial accident monitoring, volcanic ash detection, rapid air quality impact assessment

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA TEMPO mission, Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center

members.name: Aerosol Optical Properties
members.description: Comprehensive aerosol optical depth and absorbing aerosol products from multiple satellite missions providing essential information for air quality, visibility, and climate applications.

members.name: MODIS Combined Aerosol Optical Depth
members.description: Combined Terra and Aqua MODIS aerosol optical depth providing comprehensive global aerosol monitoring for air quality assessment, visibility studies, and particulate matter estimation.

info.name: Background
info.content: Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) measures the extinction of light by aerosols in the atmospheric column, providing key information about particulate matter concentrations and air quality conditions.

info.name: Combined Product Advantages
info.content: Merges Terra (morning) and Aqua (afternoon) MODIS observations for enhanced daily coverage and improved aerosol characterization with reduced data gaps

info.name: Air Quality Relationship
info.content: AOD correlates strongly with ground-level particulate matter (PM2.5 and PM10) concentrations, enabling air quality assessment in areas lacking ground-based monitoring

info.name: Spatial Resolution
info.content: 1 km resolution enabling detailed urban air quality monitoring and identification of local pollution sources

info.name: Temporal Coverage
info.content: February 2000 to present, providing over 20 years of global aerosol observations for trend analysis and climatological studies

info.name: Health Applications
info.content: PM2.5 exposure assessment, respiratory health studies, air quality index estimation, environmental health risk evaluation

info.name: Visibility Applications
info.content: Haze monitoring, visibility forecasting, transportation safety, aviation applications, tourism and recreation planning

info.name: Source Identification
info.content: Dust storm tracking, wildfire smoke detection, urban pollution monitoring, industrial emission assessment, volcanic ash monitoring

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA Terra and Aqua MODIS missions, aerosol retrieval algorithms by NASA Goddard Space Flight Center

members.name: OMI Absorbing Aerosol Optical Depth
members.description: Absorbing aerosol optical depth from OMI satellite observations, specifically detecting light-absorbing particles such as black carbon, dust, and smoke that significantly impact air quality and climate.

info.name: Background
info.content: OMI (Ozone Monitoring Instrument) Absorbing Aerosol Optical Depth specifically measures aerosols that absorb sunlight, including black carbon, dust, and smoke particles that have significant health and climate impacts.

info.name: Absorbing Aerosol Types
info.content: Detects black carbon from combustion, mineral dust from arid regions, biomass burning smoke, and other light-absorbing particles that affect air quality and climate

info.name: Health Significance
info.content: Absorbing aerosols, particularly black carbon, are associated with cardiovascular disease, respiratory problems, and cancer due to their toxic properties and small particle size

info.name: Climate Impact
info.content: Absorbing aerosols warm the atmosphere by absorbing solar radiation, contributing to regional climate change and affecting precipitation patterns

info.name: Detection Method
info.content: Uses UV observations to detect aerosols that absorb strongly in the UV spectrum, complementing visible-based aerosol retrievals

info.name: Spatial Resolution
info.content: 13 km × 24 km with daily global coverage, excellent for regional air quality and source identification

info.name: Source Monitoring
info.content: Wildfire emission tracking, diesel exhaust detection, industrial black carbon monitoring, dust storm identification, agricultural burning assessment

info.name: Environmental Justice
info.content: Identifies communities disproportionately affected by absorbing aerosol pollution, supporting environmental health equity research

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA Aura OMI mission, Royal Netherlands Meteorological Institute, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center

members.name: OMI UV Aerosol Index
members.description: UV aerosol index from OMI satellite observations providing sensitive detection of absorbing aerosols including dust, smoke, and volcanic ash affecting air quality and UV radiation transmission.

info.name: Background
info.content: The UV Aerosol Index (UVAI) is a qualitative measure of absorbing aerosols based on spectral contrast in the UV wavelength range, providing sensitive detection of dust, smoke, and volcanic particles.

info.name: Detection Sensitivity
info.content: Highly sensitive to absorbing aerosols even over bright surfaces like deserts and clouds, where traditional visible aerosol retrievals may fail

info.name: Aerosol Type Indication
info.content: Positive UVAI values indicate absorbing aerosols (dust, smoke, volcanic ash), while near-zero values suggest scattering aerosols or clean conditions

info.name: Atmospheric Hazards
info.content: Excellent for detecting atmospheric hazards including volcanic ash clouds, severe dust storms, and major wildfire smoke events that pose aviation and health risks

info.name: Global Coverage
info.content: Daily global observations with 13 km × 24 km resolution, providing comprehensive monitoring of absorbing aerosol events worldwide

info.name: Long-term Record
info.content: October 2004 to present, enabling trend analysis of dust storms, wildfire activity, and volcanic eruption impacts on air quality

info.name: Aviation Applications
info.content: Critical for aviation safety through volcanic ash detection, dust storm monitoring, and smoke plume tracking for flight path planning

info.name: Disaster Monitoring
info.content: Early warning for dust storms, wildfire smoke transport, volcanic ash dispersal, and other natural hazards affecting air quality

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA Aura OMI mission, UV aerosol index algorithm development by multiple international institutions
